requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The new feature deliberately generates a formatter for a type from a referenced assembly. Ledger L11 records that referenced-assembly types are intentionally not analysed or formatted by TypeCollector.CollectCore. The change bypasses that path, through GeneratedFormatterCollector and an explicit opt-in attribute, so L11 is not violated.

Receipts/GeneratedFormatterHonoursTypeAttributesTests.cs: edge-case test fails on head: 2/2 failed

findings.claim: Without a surrogate, the formatted type T always goes through contractless mode. Any [MessagePackObject]/[Key]/[IgnoreMember] or [DataContract]/[DataMember] attributes on T are ignored. The acceptance criterion says 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured' (the maintainer said 'If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them'). The change instead serializes every public read-write member under its name as a string key. As a result, members marked [IgnoreMember], or left out of a [DataContract], are still serialized, and [Key(int)] ordinals are replaced by name keys.

receipt_plan.detail: Run tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/GeneratedFormatterHonoursTypeAttributesTests.cs. DataContractOnReferencedTypeIsHonoured and MessagePackAttributesOnReferencedTypeAreHonoured fail on head because the generated MyTypeFormatter body references the excluded member 'Secret'.

findings.claim: Without a surrogate, the collector always uses contractless mode and never reads attributes on T. `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember(Name)]`, `[IgnoreDataMember]`, `[MessagePackObject]`/`[Key]` and `[IgnoreMember]` are all ignored. The acceptance criteria require T's attributes to be honoured. Concrete input: a referenced type `[DataContract] class MyObject { [DataMember(Name="a")] public int Included {get;set;} public int NotAMember {get;set;} }`. On head the generated formatter serializes `NotAMember` under the key "NotAMember" and `Included` under "Included" instead of "a". That breaks wire compatibility with the dynamic resolver, and members the author excluded are serialized anyway.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterLogicReceiptTests.DataContractOnReferencedTypeIsHonoured. It compiles ProjectA with the [DataContract] type into a metadata reference and runs MessagePackGenerator on ProjectB with [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]. It asserts no generated source mentions NotAMember. Expected to fail on head.

findings.claim: IsPartial checks only the formatter's own declaration. Consider a formatter nested in a non-partial containing type, for example `public class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] internal partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T> {} }`. It passes the check, and the template then emits the nesting `partial class Outer { partial class F ... }`. The result is CS0260 (missing partial modifier on Outer) instead of a MsgPack019 diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Run GeneratedFormatterLogicReceiptTests.FormatterNestedInNonPartialTypeDoesNotProduceCS0260. It asserts that the post-generation compilation has no CS0260. Expected to fail on head.

hunches.claim: The new generator filters out any class carrying [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] from hand-written formatter registration by comparing AttributeClass.ToDisplayString() to a name built from AttributeNamespace. This is only existing-user-visible if a user already has their own type with that name. It also relies on AttributeNamespace being the right namespace constant for this attribute, and the diff does not show that it is.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the generator snapshot tests with an existing hand-written formatter class and confirm the resolver output is unchanged. Also confirm AttributeNamespace equals 'MessagePack'.

hunches.claim: The generator reports diagnostics for formatters rejected by the collector, but the analyzer (MsgPack00x) never reports them. It only declares the descriptors. A formatter with a missing parameterless constructor or a mixed-key surrogate would show up as a generator diagnostic only when the generator runs. Existing projects are unaffected, so the impact is limited to the new feature.

receipt_plan.detail: Write an analyzer test with a non-partial [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class and expect MsgPack019 from the analyzer alone, without running the generator.

hunches.claim: Generated formatter for a surrogate/contractless type is emitted with the default MessagePackSecurity behavior only if the template uses the options' security; however in the user-declared partial class the generated code re-declares the base list and constraints (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>`) and member array/depth handling is unchanged. A concrete security regression is not evidenced, but string-key contractless formatters deserialize attacker-controlled map keys: the StringKey template path is reused with IsUserDeclaredFormatter and must still call options.Security.DepthStep. Reading the template is needed to confirm.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a snapshot test for [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] on a type from a referenced assembly and verify the generated Deserialize contains options.Security.DepthStep(ref reader) and reader.Depth-- in the finally, same as the existing string-key snapshot.

hunches.claim: Constructor-less handling: for structs and for classes the collector passes empty constructorParameters and always treats every member as writable/settable. Members that are init-only or required are marked IsWritable: true with IsInitOnly set. If the generator emits object-initializer or direct assignment for properties whose setter is public but init-only it is fine, but required members on contractless types are not enforced, so deserialization can silently leave required members unset. This is a correctness edge, not a security hole.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a formatter for a referenced-assembly type with a `required` public property and deserialize a map lacking that key; assert behavior/compile result.

hunches.claim: The contractless mode ignores [DataContract], [MessagePackObject] and other MessagePack attributes that T may carry. The requirement says that if T carries MessagePack attributes, they must be honoured. CreateContractlessMembers never reads attributes on T, and a type with [Key], [IgnoreMember] or [MessagePackObject] still gets name-sorted string keys.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a test where the type in the referenced assembly has [MessagePackObject] with [Key(0)]/[Key(1)] and an [IgnoreMember] member. Serialize it through a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class and assert the bytes are an integer-key array and the ignored member is skipped. The current code emits a string-key map.

hunches.claim: The contractless-vs-attributes requirement ('If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured') is implemented nowhere in the collector and untested; CreateContractlessMembers ignores [Key]/[IgnoreMember]/[DataContract] on T. No test uses an external type with attributes.

receipt_plan.detail: Add execution test with a type bearing [DataMember]/[IgnoreMember] or [MessagePackObject]+[Key] formatted via [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]; assert keys follow attributes. Expected to fail.

hunches.claim: Contractless member ordering and filter are untested beyond the single fixmap header: the OrderBy(Name) ordinal sort and IsPublicReadWrite (public fields, non-public setters, init-only, inherited members) have no tests. Fields are never exercised since all test types use properties only.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:IsPublicReadWrite IFieldSymbol branch swap-boolean: !field.IsReadOnly -> field.IsReadOnly; expected to survive because no external test type has public fields.

hunches.claim: The GeneratorUtilities guard excluding [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes from hand-written formatter registration is not directly tested; the only coverage is IsType assertions, so removal might produce a duplicate registration or a compile error that is not isolated. No snapshot test covers it.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratorUtilities.cs:37 remove-guard: delete the !symbol.GetAttributes().Any(...) clause; expected to survive or fail only through unrelated compile errors, with no targeted assertion.

hunches.claim: Missing negative and positive generator snapshot tests: no test verifies generated output for the happy path (partial class body text), the no-parameterless-constructor path, the inaccessible type path, a generic type, or surrogate duplicate keys (MsgPack006) and missing [Key] (MsgPack003). Only the mixed-key case is covered.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:~170 delete-statement: remove the claimedKeys.Add duplicate check (return null); expected to survive because no test has duplicate surrogate keys.

hunches.claim: The surrogate test only checks the array header length (8) and a round trip; it never verifies that keys 3 and 7 carry the right values, so swapping the key assignment would survive. Also a string-key surrogate path (members.Count as intKey) is untested.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:CreateSurrogateMembers off-by-one: intKey: intKey -> intKey+0 swapped for Id/Name keys; round-trip would still pass, only the header check on count exists.

hunches.claim: The MapMode execution test project excludes the new tests, so the template change for IsUserDeclaredFormatter in the string-key template is only exercised via contractless; the int-key FormatterTemplate branch is covered only by the surrogate test. Existing snapshot tests for non-user formatters are not shown to check unchanged output.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the generator snapshot tests to confirm the template edit leaves existing 'internal sealed class' output byte-identical.

hunches.claim: No accessibility check is made on the formatter class itself. A `private partial class F` nested in another type is accepted and registered in the generated resolver. The resolver cannot instantiate it, so compilation fails with CS0122 (inaccessible) instead of a generator diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Collect validates only IsSymbolAccessibleWithin(type, formatter) for the data type, never the formatter's own accessibility relative to the resolver. Compare with MsgPack012 handling for data types.

hunches.claim: GetInstanceMembers keeps only the most-derived member of each name. Take a derived class that overrides only the getter (`public override int X { get => ...; }`) of a base read-write property. Its IPropertySymbol has SetMethod == null, so IsPublicReadWrite returns false and the base's writable X is shadowed by the `seen` set. The member is silently dropped from the contractless contract, although the property is writable through the base setter.

receipt_plan.detail: GetInstanceMembers adds the derived override to `seen` before visiting the base. IsPublicReadWrite then requires property.SetMethod to be non-null, and an override with only a get accessor has none.

hunches.claim: New analyzer diagnostics MsgPack019-022 are added to SupportedDiagnostics, but the analyzer tracking file (AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md) and doc pages are not in the diff. RS2000 may break the build, and help links point to missing docs.

receipt_plan.detail: Check that AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md lists MsgPack019-022 and that doc/analyzers/MsgPack019.md through MsgPack022.md exist. Otherwise build the analyzer project with warnings-as-errors and look for RS2000.

hunches.claim: The README tells users to write the attribute as written, while the new attribute lives in MessagePack.Annotations. The README example shows `[Key]` and `[IgnoreMember]` on a surrogate. The README also documents MsgPack019 to MsgPack022 as the diagnostics. Diagnostics MsgPack005, MsgPack004 (NoDeserializingConstructor) and MsgPack003 (MemberNeedsKey) are reused from existing descriptors, with misleading messages, and the doc pages for them are not updated. This is a minor doc inconsistency.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratedFormatterCollector reuses MemberNeedsKey, DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys, KeysMustBeUnique and NoDeserializingConstructor, but the README says diagnostics are MsgPack019 to MsgPack022 only.

hunches.claim: MsgPack019 to MsgPack022 are reported only from the generator via RegisterSourceOutput, not from the analyzer. The analyzer's SupportedDiagnostics lists the descriptors but the analyzer never reports them. This diverges from the convention that MsgPack0xx diagnostics come from the analyzer. IDE code fixes and disabling via analyzer configuration may behave differently.

receipt_plan.detail: Compare MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.Initialize, which has no registration for GeneratedMessagePackFormatter, with the generator's context.ReportDiagnostic call at MessagePackGenerator.cs:131.

narrative: This run reviews reading A of REQ-2129 on branch review/ju26-issue-2129/A: Contractless means only public, non-static, read-write instance properties and fields, serialized with string keys equal to their names. Deserialization requires an accessible parameterless constructor (classes). Getter-only members are skipped, and types that have only a parameterized constructor are rejected (GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs:77 and CreateContractlessMembers using IsPublicReadWrite).
